source.text: ወእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ እቤ፡ ዝንቱ፡ ሠናይ፡ ዕፀ፡ ወ†*ሠናይ፡ ለርእይ፡† ወአዳም፡ ቈጽሉ፡ ወ†ፍሬሁኒ፡† ሞገስ፡ ጥቀ፡ ለርእዩ፡ ገጽ።
source.note: Unapplied candidate adjusted to the apparent printed opening ወእተ on Charles1906 printed p62/PDF100. Verify exact full glyphs against high-resolution primary detail; no canonical or manuscript claim.

translation.text: Then I said, “This is a beautiful tree, beautiful to look at[a]; its leaves are lovely, and its fruit[b] is very pleasing to look at.”

footnotes.text: The printed Ethiopic appearance expression is asterisked and dagger-marked. Charles p62 note9 considers the Greek fragrance reading preferable, but this English follows his printed Ethiopic appearance wording.
The printed fruit expression is dagger-marked. Charles p62 note10 calls it corrupt and proposes flowers by comparison with Greek; “fruit” follows the selected main line.

source.text: ወእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ አውሥአኒ፡ ሚካኤል፡ ፩እምነ፡ መላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ወክቡራን፡ እንዘ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ሀሎ፡ ውእቱ፡ ዘዲቤሆሙ።
source.note: Unapplied candidate adjusted to the apparent printed opening ወእተ on Charles1906 printed p62/PDF100. Verify exact full glyphs against high-resolution primary detail; no canonical or manuscript claim.

translation.text: Then Michael, one of the holy and honored angels who was with me, answered me—he who was over them.[a]

footnotes.text: Michael is the subject of the accompanying and over-them clauses, but the plural referent is unnamed here. “Honored” can also be “glorious”; p62 note15 records omission in Greek, not in this selected Ethiopic. His speech begins only in chapter25.
